To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) windstorms do great damage to banana plantations near Santa Marta, 2) most of this damage is triggered by large-scale atmospheric disturbances, 3) seeding to reduce storm intensity is feasible, 4) seeding is likely to be economically rewarding.
the windstorms were triggered by easterlies and that cloud-seeding experiments to reduce the severity of the storms were unsuccessful.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the windstorms of the 1956–1957 seasons in the banana plantations near Santa Marta were of a type that could not have been mitigated by any of the techniques of cloud seeding that were used, and that the damage caused by these windstorms was not significantly different from that of the previous 10 years.

we have shown that the windstorms of this region are a real problem, that the damage they cause is not only great but also highly concentrated in time and space, that the windstorms are triggered by large-scale disturbances, and that the windstorms themselves are purely local, and that seeding has not been effective in mitigating the windstorms.

the use of a single, global, and uniform threshold for the definition of a tropical cyclone is problematic.
